why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)
a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

no.txt: names a domain, not what follows

Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)
the case names the meaning — “in the sense of X”

no.txt: names a meaning, not what follows

left.txt: a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — क्स: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”
a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — it replaces the WHOLE of the place

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A 7th-case word naming a following sound, suffix or word (“… परे”) puts the operation on what comes immediately before it. Not a 7th naming a meaning or domain (आर्धधातुके as ‘in its sphere’); if the rule also has a 5th, the 5th wins. (Bhāṣya: “शब्दे सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टे पूर्वस्य कार्यं यथा स्यात्। अर्थे मा भूत्।”)

teaching_view.fin: उप-पूर्वात् सृ-धातोः यत्-प्रत्ययान्तः स्त्रीलिङ्गः उपसर्या इति निपात्यते काल्या (प्राप्तकाला) चेत् प्रजने (प्रथमगर्भग्रहणे)
teaching_view.note: Why a nipātana: सृ ends in ऋ, so normally it would take ण्यत् (3.1.124 ऋहलोर्ण्यत्) and give उपसार्या, with vṛddhi. The references show this through the counter-example — Kāśikā: “काल्या प्रजन इति किम्? उपसार्या शरदि मधुरा”; SK: “उपसार्या काशी । प्राप्तव्येत्यर्थः” — without naming 3.1.124. This sūtra states उपसर्या (with यत्, no vṛddhi) only for a female whose time has come for her first conception (SK: “गर्भग्रहणे प्राप्तकाला चेदित्यर्थः”). Examples (Kāśikā): उपसर्या गौः, उपसर्या वडवा.

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. quote.q: Thus विक्षिप् + क = विक्षिप nom. sing. विक्षिपः. So also विलिखः 'inscription'; बुधः 'who knows', कृशः 'lean'; ज्ञा + क = ज्ञः 'who knows' [[6.4.64]]; प्री + क = प्रियः 'what pleases'; कॄ + क = कि + अ ( VII.I.100) = किर् + अ [[1.1.51]] = किरः 'who scatters' i. e. 'a hog'.

why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)
पुरा here means the word पुरा itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”
it describes another word of the rule

no.txt: names a qualification, not what follows

why.txt: विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — it replaces the WHOLE of the place

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
the case names the meaning — “in the sense of X”

why.txt: it describes another word of the rule

quote.q: <<क्क्ङिति च>>[[१.१.५]] इत्यत्र गकारोऽपि चर्त्वभूतो निर्दिश्यते, तेन गुणो न भवति
यदि तर्हि गिदयम्, जिष्णुरित्यत्र गुणः प्राप्नोति, यस्मात् <<क्ङिति च>> [[1.1.5]]  इति क्ङिति प्रत्यये गुणः प्रतिषिध्यते, न गितीत्यत आह -  `क्ङिति च` इत्यादि
गित् कित् ङिदिति त्रिषु गुणाभावः स्मर्तव्यः;'क्ङिति च'  इत्यत्र गकारप्रश्लेषात्
ककारे गकार्रश्चत्वभूतौ निर्दिश्यते - क्क्ङिति चेति
क्क्ङिति चे॑त्यत्र गस्य चर्त्वेन ककारान्तरप्रश्लेषादिति भावः
क्ङिति चे॑त्यत्र गकारं प्रश्लिष्य गिति किति ङितीति व्याख्यानादिति भाव-

In the sutra (l. 1.5.) (क्ङिति च) the letter ग is also included; for ग coming before क, is changed by the rules of sandhi into क and is not therefore visible. This affix therefore does not cause guna.

quote.q: ननु मादीत्यत्र चरितार्थमेतत्, उत्पूर्वात्वलंकृञादिसूत्रेण विशेषविहित इष्णुजेव प्राप्नोति, वाऽसरूपविधिना घिनुण् भविष्यति, ताच्छीलिकेषु वाऽसरूपविधिर्नास्तीत्येततु प्रायिकमिति वक्ष्यते
उत्पूर्वान्मदेः अलंकृञादिसूत्रेणेष्णुजुक्तो वासरूपविधिना घिनुणपि
ननु कथमत्र ताच्छीलिके घिनुणि वाऽसरूपविधिप्रवृत्तिः,ताच्छीलिकेषु वाऽसरूपविधिर्नास्ती॑ति निषेधादित्यत आह —  ताच्छीलिकेष्विति

As शमिन् Ist. sing. शमी 'calm'; likewise तमी 'desiring'; दमी 'taming'; श्रमी 'laborious'; भ्रमी 'whirling', 'moving round'; क्लमी 'fatiguing'; क्षमी 'forbearing'; प्रमादी 'mad' and उन्मादी 'mad'. Though by rule 136, the verb उन्मद takes the affix इष्णुच्, it also takes the affix घिनुण् by the rule o

why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. cards.ans: लप सृ द्रु मथ वद वस इत्येतेभ्यः धातुभ्यः

why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

quote.q: ण्वुलैव सिद्धे वुञ्विधानं ज्ञापनार्थम् — ताच्छीलिकेषु वासरूपन्यायेन तृजादयो न भवन्ति (महाभाष्य २.१३३) इति

अथ किमर्थं निन्दादिभ्यो धातुभ्यो वुञ् विधीयते, यावता वाऽसरूपविधिनैव निन्दकादयः,सिद्धाः, तदेव हि रूपम्, स एव स्वरः, इहैवैकत्र स्वरविशेषोऽस्ति -  असूयक इति, अत्र वुञि सति ञित्वादादेरुदात्तत्वं भवति, ण्वुलि तु सति लित्प्रत्ययात् पूर्वस्य स्यात्, तस्मादसूयतेरेवैकस्माद्वुञ्, विधातव्यः, नेतरेभ्यो निन्दादि
तस्मादेवैकस्माद् वुञ् विधेयः, अन्येभ्यस्तु ण्वुलैव सिद्धम्, योऽयं तच्छीलादिषु तृन्विधीयते स बाधकः प्राप्नोति, वाऽसरूपविधिना ण्वुलपि भविष्यति, तत्राह - ण्वुलैव सिद्ध इति
(आक्षेपसाधकभाष्यम्) वाऽसरूपेण न्यायेन ण्वुलपि भविष्यति
तच्छीलादिषु वासरूपविदिस्त्तवे हि तद्विषये तृनि प्राप्ते वुञ्विधिरर्थवान्

quote.q: ज्ञापकार्थं च पदिग्रहणमन्ये वर्णयन्ति — <<ताच्छीलिकेषु मिथो वासरूपविधिर्नास्ति>> इति
यदि ताच्छीलिके वाऽसरूपविधिः स्यात् ततोऽसरूपत्वदेवोकञा समावेशः स्यादिति पदेर्युज्विधानमनर्थकं स्यात्
यथाह - पदिग्रहणमनर्थकमनुदातेतश्च हलादेरिरि सिद्धत्वात्? वासरूपनिवृत्यर्थ त्विति
वासरूपन्यायेन युजपि भविष्यति
तेन ताच्छीलिकेषु परस्परं वासरूपविधिर्नास्तीति
तत्र वाऽसरूपविधिनैव उकञाअनुदात्तेतश्च हलादे॑रिति विहितस्य पदेर्युचो बाधो न भविष्यतीति 'जुचङ्क्रम्ये' ति युज्विधिरनर्थकः स्यादतस्तातच्छीलिकेषु परस्परं वासरूपविधिर्नास्तीति विज्ञायते इत्यर्थः
निन्दादिसूत्रे हि तच्चीलादिषु वासरूपविधिना तृजादयो नेति ज्ञापितम्, इह तुताच्छीलिकेषु परस्परं ने॑ति ज्ञापितमिति विवेक इति भावः

The enumeration of the word पद in the above, indicates that this sutra applies to the transitive verbs; otherwise the sutra [[3.2.148]] would have been sufficient, as पद is a चलनार्थ verb. Others say that the inclusion of पद् in this aphorism indicates the existence of the paribhash

quote.q: स एव बाधको भविष्यति, किं प्रतिषेधेन? वासरूपेण युजपि प्राप्नोति
`वाऽसरूपेण` इत्यादि परिहारः
ननुताच्छीलिकेषु वासरूपविधिर्नास्तीति ज्ञापितम्, तत्कथं वाऽसरूपेण युजिह प्राप्नोति? तत्राह - ताच्छीलिकेष्विति
नमिकम्पि - <{SK3147}> इति रेण युचो बाधे सिद्धे दीपेर्ग्रहणं ज्ञापयति ताच्छीलिकेषु वासरूपविधिर्नास्तीति प्रायिकमिति
नच वाऽसरूपविधिना तद्बाधः शङ्क्यः, ताच्छीलिकेषु वासरूपविधेः प्रतिषेधादित्यत आह —  नमिकम्पीति

Now, it might be objected-- "We find that sutra [[3.2.167]] specifically enjoins the affix र after दीप्; this apavada rule will therefore, supersede the general rule; where is then the necessity of the present rule? If you say that the affix युच् is also obtained by the rule of non-uni

quote.q: स्यादेतत् -  वाऽसरूपविधिना क्वचिदपि भविष्यतीत्याह -  `वाऽसरूपविधिश्च` इति

Thus, विभ्राज् Ist. sing. विभ्राट् 'splendid'; भास् Ist. sing. भाः 'light'; धुर्व् + क्विप् = धुर् [[6.4.21]], Ist sing. धूः 'who injures'; विद्युत् 'lightening'; ऊर्ज Ist. sing. कर्क् 'strength'; पुर् Ist. sing. पूः 'what fills'; जूः 'swift'. In the case of जु, a long vowel is the substitute of जु;

a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE — it replaces the WHOLE of the place

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)

why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

why.txt: In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)
the case names the meaning — “in the sense of X”

no.txt: names a meaning, not what follows

why.txt: विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

quote.q: ततश्च <<तपरस्तत्कालस्य>> [[1.1.70]]  इति परिभाषोपस्थानादिहैव स्यात् -  यवः,स्तव इति; लवः,पव इत्यत्र तु न स्यात्

The द् in ॠद् is merely for the sake of euphony: it is not त् changed into द; for then by the rule 'that which follows त् is also called तपर' short उ only would have been taken and not long ऊ [[1.1.70]].

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

why.txt: Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

quote.q: वासरूपप्रतिषेधश्च स्त्रीप्रकरणविषयस्यैवोत्सर्गापवादस्य

ननु च वासरूपविधिना ण्यत्प्रत्ययः स्यात्, स च वासरूपविधिः स्त्रियां न भवति, `अस्त्रियाम्`  [[3.1.94]]  इति प्रतिषेधात्, तत् किमुच्यते -  `ऋहलोण्र्यत्`  [[3.1.124]]  इति ण्यद्भविष्य(ती)ति? इत्यत आह -  `वासरूप` इत्यादि
ननु वासरूपविधिना ण्यत्स्यात् स चास्त्रियामिति प्रतिषिद्धः ? तत्राह - वासरूपप्रतिषेधश्चेति
न च स्त्रीप्रत्यये वाऽसरूपविधिर्नेति शङ्क्यम्, अपवादस्य युचः स्त्रीप्करणस्थत्वेऽपि उत्सर्गस्य ण्यतस्तदभावात्

This excludes the affix अ [[3.1.102]]. Thus कृ + णिच् = कारि; कारि + युच् = कारणा (the इ is elided by [[6.4.51]]) 'the causing to do'; हारणा 'the causing to take'; आसना 'the sitting'; श्रन्थना 'the loosening'. How do we get the form आस्या ? It is the feminine of आस्य formed by adding ण्यत् to the ro

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

why.txt: विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)
कथं here means the word कथं itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

quote.q: वासरूपविधिना भविष्यन्ति? एवं तर्हि ज्ञापयति — स्त्र्यधिकारात् परेण वासरूपविधिर्नावश्यं भवतीति
`वासरूप`इत्यादीना परीहारं विघटयति
(कृत्यसाधकभाष्यम्) वासरूपेण कृत्या अपि भविष्यन्ति

It might be asked 'Why the kritya affixes are enjoined to come with the force of direction, permission &c'. They have been ordained most generically to come in denoting action in the Abstract (भाव) and object (कर्म) and a fortiori they will come in denoting the senses of direction, permission

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

why.txt: the suffix named in the 1st case is what is introduced

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)
ईश्वर here means the word ईश्वर itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

The phrase 'in the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians' shows that it is an optional rule. Therefore we have अलंरोदनेन 'do not weep'. Or if rule [[3.1.94]] be applied, then the use of the word प्राचां is for the sake of merely showing respect (pujartha); the rule could have stood without it.

quote.q: ननु च वासरूप इति भविष्यति? क्त्वाणमुलौ यत्र सह विधीयेते तत्र वासरूपविधिर्नास्तीत्येतदनेन ज्ञाप्यते
यस्तु `समानकर्त्तृकयोः`  [[3.4.21]]  इत्यादिना केवलः क्त्वा विहितस्तं प्रति विभाषाग्रहणं न कर्तव्यमेव; वासरूपविधिना तत्प्रतिपादितस्यार्थस्य सिद्धत्वात्

नन्वेवं णमुल्यप्राप्ते क्त्वाप्रत्यये तु'समानकर्तृकयोः'  इत्यादिना प्राप्ते सत्ययमारम्भ इति पुनरप्युभयत्रविभाषैव युक्ता ? नैतदस्ति; सह विहितौ यौ क्त्वाणमुलौ यद्विषये वासरूपविधेरभावो ज्ञापयितुमिष्टः, तावनन्तरसूत्रविहितौ क्त्वाणमुलावभिप्रेत्याप्राप्तविभाषेयमुच्यते, न तु क्त्वाणमुल्मात्रपेक्षया
Q-- The affixes of Lat (Present tense) &c. would have been applied by the rule of वाऽसरूप [[3.1.94]]; why then use the word 'optionally'?

why.txt: In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

विभाषा names ‘not’ and ‘optionally’ together, so the rule's operation is optional; वा and अन्यतरस्याम् work the same way. A carried option word counts only where it is still in force (the commentary may call a rule nitya). बहुलम् is wider than an option. (Kāśikā: “विभाषाधिकारेऽपि नित्यसमास एवायम्।”)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)

why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)
नामन् here means the word नामन् itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

A suffix named as a known element stands for the word from the base it was added to up to that suffix (सन् → सन्नन्त). Not in saṃjñā rules or the uttarapada section, nor when the rule teaches or changes that suffix; as a 7th-case condition it means ‘what begins with it’. (Śekhara: “संज्ञाविधौ … तदन्तग्रहणं नास्ति”)

why.txt: a suffix is placed AFTER its base (परश्च, under the प्रत्ययः heading 3.1.1–5.4.160)

In the dhātu section (3.1.91 to the end of book 3) what a sūtra names in the 7th case is the upapada, the word used with the dhātu; the suffix comes only when it is there. A 7th stating the suffix's meaning (कर्मणि in धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्) is not an upapada. (Bālamanoramā: “सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति”)
तिर्यक् here means the word तिर्यक् itself, not its meaning or its synonyms — काशिका on 1.1.68: “शास्त्रे स्वमेव रूपं शब्दस्य ग्राह्यं बोध्यं प्रत्याय्यं भवति, न बाह्योऽर्थः”

why.txt: A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)

why.txt: the substitute stands in the 1st case — Mahābhāṣya on 1.1.57: “आदेशः प्रथमानिर्दिष्टः”

Where a rule teaches a substitute, a 6th-case word whose link is otherwise unclear names what is replaced (“… स्थाने”). Not in augment rules (the 6th is the host), not where another word names the part replaced (उपधायाः, एचः), not where no substitute is taught. (Bhāṣya: “सन्देहे नियमः।”)
when two lists have the same number of members they pair up IN ORDER (yathāsaṅkhya) — they pair up in order (यथासङ्ख्यम्)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
when two lists have the same number of members they pair up IN ORDER (yathāsaṅkhya) — they pair up in order (यथासङ्ख्यम्)

a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः [= च तदन्तविधिः], न विशेष्येण”)

A 5th-case word of direction (‘after X’) puts the operation on what comes immediately after it — something already there (substitute, augment, elision, accent). Placing a new suffix is 3.1.2; a 5th of cause or ‘other than’, or an explicit पूर्व, is not this rule. (Kāśikā: “पञ्चम्यर्थनिर्देश उत्तरस्यैव कार्यं भवति”)
